name: Phoebe, plantation-grown (楠木, Phoebe zhennan and P. bournei)
aliases: 金丝楠 (golden-thread nanmu, the chatoyant grade)
summary: The finest of Chinese building and furniture timbers: a fragrant, stable, fine-grained golden wood of the laurel family whose best grade shows a moving chatoyance (金丝, golden thread). Now protected, it is plantation-grown. In Chenghuai it is the main hall's carved screens (花罩), every case plinth and the tables, waxed and never painted.

species.text: Nanmu is produced by several trees (Litsea cubeba, Machilus nanmu, Phoebe hungmaoensis, Phoebe zhennan); the genus Phoebe produces the highest grades.

whyAnAccent.text: Principle 2 names one oak. Chenghuai is built as it would be in Beijing, and its approved Materials board names Korean pine, Chinese fir and plantation Phoebe. Each is declared an accent of the oak family (D-014): timber in the oak's role, tied to it by value and hue under its finish. The Architect may overturn this reading.
whyAnAccent.source: MuseeVision/Journal/Decisions.md, D-014 (Matter: every substance carries its family; an accent names its core family); plan/proposals/chenghuai/canvas/Materials.dc.html (approved Chenghuai proposal: '營造')

plantation.text: Officially protected in China; deforestation, disease and pollution have almost exhausted the wild trees; small populations remain in protected artificial forests and ornamental plantings.

designChoice.text: 楠木 Phoebe, plantation-grown: 正房 screens, every case plinth; waxed, never painted.

formation.how: A slow-growing evergreen of the laurel family. Its wood is diffuse-porous with small vessels and short fibres, fine and even in texture, fragrant, and dries with little splitting or warping. Premium wood is bright golden with a wavy or quilted figure and a strong chatoyance, the 'golden thread'; light, loose-grained wood is the lesser grade. Young plantation stems have not yet formed a distinct heartwood.

character.text: Bright golden colour, a pleasant fragrance and impressive chatoyancy, hence 'golden thread'; a wavy or quilted grain figure; dries with little splitting or warping; can be sanded to a mirror finish; does not react much to humidity and temperature by expansion or contraction.

cellWallRefractiveIndex.source: Marschner, S.R., Westin, S.H., Arbree, A. & Moon, J.T. (2005) Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood. ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3), 727-734, https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073254 (https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/SG05-wood-lr.pdf)
cellWallRefractiveIndex.note: the cell wall treated as one homogeneous dielectric ('cellulose'), following Saarinen and Muinonen (2001) for paper fibres; a modelling value, not a measured index of oak

fibreHighlight.text: Finished wood shows a subsurface highlight that no surface-anisotropy model reproduces: light enters, scatters from the aligned fibres below the surface and leaves on a cone about the local fibre axis, which can tilt out of the surface plane. The model adds a fibre term (fibre axis u, fibre colour k_f, and a Gaussian highlight width beta, one per species) to a Fresnel-corrected diffuse term and the finish's own surface specular; both subsurface terms are attenuated by Fresnel transmission in and out through the finish. On interlocked grain the highlight swings 30-40 degrees either side of the normal across the figure. Measured samples: varnished walnut, lacquered walnut, lacquered curly maple, varnished padauk; oak was not measured.
fibreHighlight.source: Marschner, S.R., Westin, S.H., Arbree, A. & Moon, J.T. (2005) Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood. ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3), 727-734, https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073254 (https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/SG05-wood-lr.pdf)

optics.chatoyance: The 'golden thread' is the fibre highlight of Marschner et al. on a figured grain: where the fibre direction undulates or interlocks, the highlight swings across the figure as the view moves (30-40 degrees either side of the normal on interlocked padauk). A wax finish, index close to the cell wall's, lets it show.

unfinishedSurfaceScatter.text: Planing and sanding leave a layer of broken cells whose irregular surface scatters white light diffusely, which is why unfinished wood looks light and unsaturated; a clear finish whose index is close to the cell wall's removes that first interface, so colour deepens and the subsurface highlight appears.

photograph: A warm gold-brown, finer and closer than oak, no open pores; a satin wax sheen.
Bands of light and dark that trade places as you move (the golden thread), strongest on quarter-cut boards and carved curves.
Crisp carving with slightly softened high points where hands and cloths have polished them.

unverified.field: physical.density of mature Phoebe zhennan heartwood
unverified.reason: The measured values are for 14-year-old P. bournei thinnings with no heartwood; mature nanmu is denser (about 610 kg/m3 air-dry is often quoted from the Chinese timber record 中国木材志, which was not read).
That the golden thread is the fibre highlight on interlocked or wavy grain follows Marschner et al.'s measurements on other species; no measurement of phoebe was read.
No measured colour of plantation or mature phoebe was read.
